output.brief: The drop is mainly caused by a new edge rule, not by customers or the 6.14 password screen. Corvane's rule pack, auto-applied on 3 March at 10:38 UTC, added AUTO-LIB-17, which blocks requests from the 'nettle-http' library on the password-login path. Android 6.14 uses that library (bumped in 6.14), so real Android password logins are being blocked with a 403 at the edge. Blocks start within minutes of the rule going live, are zero on iOS, web and quick-unlock, and the blocked requests come from installed-app IDs that mostly logged in successfully before. Credential stuffing and the auth-service change don't fit this pattern. I'm fairly confident in the mechanism, less so in the exact share of the drop it explains. Next: ask Corvane to set AUTO-LIB-17 to log-only on the mobile password path, keeping rate limits, lockout and other rules, and confirm recovery in telemetry. Don't exclude blocked attempts from the KPI, raise bot sensitivity, or continue the rollout unchanged. Plan a durable fix with Mobile and Corvane. Revisit the password-screen revert only if the rule fix doesn't restore success.
